English language requirements

Search our courses
Search our courses

Find out about the level of English language you need to study at CCCU.

As an international student, you must hold a relevant English Language qualification alongside your academic qualifications to apply for a Student Route visa.

Here you will find a list of English language tests, as well as their requirements for our undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.

English language qualifications

Run by the British Council, the IELTS test is the most widely recognised and commonly available English language qualification.

IELTS indicator/academic tests

IELTS Indicator is an online test that can be taken in-person or online. The test includes four skills: Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking. You will receive an indicative score for each. Your performance will be marked by IELTS examiners and you will receive your result within seven days.

Course type IELTS Indicator requirements (where appropriate)
Standard undergraduate and postgraduate programmes 6.0 overall with no element below 5.5
Professional health undergraduate programmes (including Nursing courses starting in 2026)

7.0 overall with no element below 6.5
Nursing undergraduate programmes starting 2027 onwards

6.5 overall with no element below 6.5
Non-standard postgraduate programmes 6.5 overall with no element below 6.0

Taken in-person, the PTE test is designed to test international English. There are three parts to the overall test: Speaking and Writing, Reading, and Listening. You will take the online test in a test centre, and your score will be sent to you within five working days.

For further information please visit the Pearson website.

Course type Pearson PTE score requirements (where appropriate)
Standard undergraduate and postgraduate programmes 59 overall with no element below 59
Professional health undergraduate programmes

76 overall with no element below 76
Non-standard postgraduate programmes 56 overall with no element below 46

The TOEFL IBT can be taken either in-person or online. We cannot accept the TOEFL IBT home test.  There are four tests to complete: Reading, Listening, Speaking, and Writing.

The entire test will take around 3.5 hours to complete, including a 30 minute break. You'll receive your score within four days of completion.

For further information please visit the TOEFL website.

Course type TOEFL IBT score requirements (where appropriate) TOEFL IBT SCORE requirements for tests taken from January 21st 2026
Standard undergraduate and postgraduate programmes Minimum of 60 overall: Reading 8, Listening 7, Speaking 16 and Writing 18 Minimum of 4 overall: Reading 4, Listening 4, Speaking 4 and Writing 4.
Professional health undergraduate programmes

Minimum of 94 overall: Reading 19, Listening 20, Speaking 20, and Writing 24

Minimum of  5 overall: Reading 4.5, Listening 4.5, Speaking 4.5, and Writing 4.5
Non-standard postgraduate programmes

Minimum of 79 overall: Reading 13, Listening 12, Speaking 18 and Writing 21

 Minimum of  5 overall: Reading 4.5, Listening 4.5, Speaking 4.5, and Writing 4.5

Country specific exemptions

We are able to waive the English language requirement for certain countries and qualifications. Please check your country or region to see if you are eligible.

English language courses at CCCU 

If you do not currently have the English language qualifications to study at CCCU, you can take an English language course to prepare you for university level study. 

The International Foundation Programme is designed to help you improve your English language skills to degree level to prepare you for your studies.

You will learn English to a higher level, preparing you for your chosen course once you have finished the International Foundation Programme. 

You will also learn from lecturers and complete assessments that will be similar to your degree.

For this English language course, you will need a Secure English Language Test, know as a SELT. This can include:

  • IELTS for UKVI
  • Pearson PTE Academic UKVI
  • LanguageCert SELT.

If you are applying to study an undergraduate degree that includes a professional qualification - such as Nursing - you may have to pass additional admission requirements, such as an interview. 

If you would like to talk about the entry requirements you need for this course, please contact Admissions. 

If you have met the English language requirements to study with CCCU but would like to further your language skills before starting your undergraduate course, you can complete a six or ten week online course called the Pre-sessional course in Academic English Skills.

You can also take this course if you already hold an IELTS qualification but it doesn't quite meet the requirements for the degree you want to study. 

The amount of weeks you need for this pre-sessional course depends on your current IELTS qualification. 

Entry requirements for the pre-sessional online course

Unlike the International Foundation Programme, you will not need a Secure English Language Test (SELT). However, you will need to meet the following criteria in order to join the course. 

English language level requirement for your degree / study programme

Entry level requirement for 10-week Pre-sessional Course

Entry level requirement for 6-week Pre-sessional Course

Standard undergraduate and postgraduate programmes

IELTS 6.0 overall with 6.0 in writing and no element below 5.5

5.0 overall with a minimum of 4.5 in all elements

5.5 overall with a minimum of 5.0 in all elements

Non-standard postgraduate programmes (Psychology, Applied Linguistics)

IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing and no element below 6.0

5.5 overall with a minimum of 5.0 in all elements

6.0 overall with a minimum of 5.5 in all elements

If you successfully pass this course, this will count as meeting the English language requirement so you can start undergraduate study.

If you would like to talk about the entry requirements you need for this course, please contact Admissions. 

 

The General English Course will prepare you for life in the UK as you gain confidence speaking English and living in Canterbury. 

Available throughout the year, you can choose to take a full year's course or two weeks - this will depend on your personal circumstances and levels of English. 

Accredited by the British Council, you will finish the course with the skills and confidence to speak English and navigate life in the UK.

  • Diagnostic Radiography

  • Postgraduate Admissions Team.
